# Shoulder and axilla

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Rheumatology and immunology > Basics of rheumatology > Shoulder and axilla*

[Original Article Link](/library/cK0a2S)

---

## Summary

The upper limb bones and <u>shoulder girdle</u> form the superior <u>appendicular skeleton</u>. Four <u>joints</u> (glenohumeral, sternoclavicular, acromioclavicular, and scapulothoracic) and two bones (the <u>clavicle</u> and <u>scapula</u>) form the <u>shoulder girdle</u>. The <u>glenohumeral joint</u> (i.e., <u>shoulder joint</u>) is one of the most flexible <u>joints</u> in the body and relies on a <u>complex system</u> of muscles, including the <u>rotator cuff</u>, to keep it in shape and enable mobility. Branches of the subclavian and <u>axillary arteries</u> supply the entire upper extremity. <u>Veins</u> of the upper extremity drain into the <u>axillary vein</u>, and <u>lymphatics</u> of the upper extremity drain into the <u>axillary lymph node groups</u>. The branches of the <u>brachial plexus</u> supply the motor and sensory innervation of the upper extremity. The <u>axilla</u> is a three-dimensional pyramid-shaped area at the junction of the arm and thorax, inferior to the <u>shoulder joint</u>, through which important vessels and nerves pass from the trunk to the arm.




For more information, see “<u>Neurovasculature of the upper limbs</u>,” “<u>Upper arm and elbow</u>,” and “<u>Forearm, wrist, and hand</u>.”

## Shoulder girdle

* Definition: a bony ring that connects the upper limb to the <u>axial skeleton</u>

* Bones  [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)

* <u>Clavicle</u>

* <u>Scapula</u>

* <u>Joints</u> ;   [[2]](/library/XNY9-6)

* True anatomical <u>joints</u> (movement occurs between two directly articulating skeletal structures)

* <u>Acromioclavicular joint</u>

* <u>Sternoclavicular joint</u>

* <u>Glenohumeral joint</u>

* Physiologic <u>joint</u>: <u>scapulothoracic joint</u>

## Bones of the shoulder girdle

### Clavicle  [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




* Definition: an S-shaped bone that connects the <u>scapula</u> to the <u>sternum</u>, located above and <u>anterior</u> to the first <u>rib</u>

* <u>Joints</u>

* Sternal end (<u>medial</u>): articulates with the <u>manubrium</u> of the <u>sternum</u> to form the <u>sternoclavicular joint</u>

* Acromial end (<u>lateral</u>): articulates with the <u>acromion</u> of the <u>scapula</u> to form the <u>acromioclavicular joint</u>

* Muscle attachments

* <u>Lateral</u> one-third: <u>trapezius</u> and <u>deltoid muscles</u>

* <u>Medial</u> two-thirds: <u>sternocleidomastoid</u>, <u>pectoralis major</u>, and <u>subclavius muscles</u>

* Surface markings

* Subclavian groove

* A groove on the inferior surface of the middle third of the <u>clavicle</u>

* The <u>subclavius muscle</u> attaches here.

* Impression for costoclavicular ligament (<u>medial</u>)

* A rough depressed oval area on the <u>medial</u> third of the <u>clavicle</u>

* The <u>costoclavicular ligament</u> attaches here, binding the first <u>rib</u> to the <u>clavicle</u> and limiting shoulder elevation.

* Tuberosity for coracoclavicular ligament (<u>lateral</u>)

* Formed by the <u>conoid tubercle</u> and the <u>trapezoid line</u>

* The site for attachment of the two parts of the <u>coracoclavicular ligament</u> (the conoid and <u>trapezoid ligaments</u>)

* Conoid tubercle: <u>conoid ligament</u> insertion point

* Trapezoid line: <u>trapezoid ligament</u> insertion point





![Clavicle (anatomical)](media/z9tv4ropznkf29vhtcrye26q.jpg)

Clavicle (anatomical)




### Scapula  [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




* Definition: a flat and triangular-shaped bone that overlies the 2<sup>nd</sup>–7<sup>th</sup><u>posterior</u> <u>ribs</u>.

* Borders: <u>medial</u>, <u>lateral</u>/axillary, and superior

* Angles: superior, inferior, and <u>lateral</u>

* Surfaces

* <u>Posterior</u> surface

* Spine of scapula

* Horizontal bony ridge that divides the <u>posterior</u> scapular surface into the <u>supraspinous fossa</u> and <u>infraspinous fossa</u>

* The <u>deltoid muscle</u> attaches to the deltoid tubercle on the <u>scapular spine</u>.

* Acromion

* <u>Lateral</u> continuation of the <u>scapular spine</u> that projects above the <u>glenoid fossa</u>

* Articulates with the acromial end of the <u>clavicle</u>

* Supraspinous fossa

* <u>Concave</u> <u>depression</u> above the <u>scapular spine</u>

* The <u>supraspinatus muscle</u> attaches here.

* Infraspinous fossa

* <u>Concave</u> <u>depression</u> below the <u>scapular spine</u>

* The <u>infraspinatus muscle</u> attaches here.

* Costal (<u>anterior</u>) surface

* Subscapular fossa

* <u>Concave</u> <u>depression</u> on the body of the <u>scapula</u>

* The <u>subscapularis muscle</u> attaches here.

* Coracoid process

* Anteriorly projecting bony hook that arises from the superior border of the <u>scapula</u>

* Lies below the <u>lateral</u> end of the <u>clavicle</u>, in close proximity to the <u>brachial plexus</u> and axillary vessels

* The <u>pectoralis minor</u>, <u>coracobrachialis</u>, and short head of the <u>biceps brachii muscles</u> attach here.

* Suprascapular notch

* A deep groove between the <u>coracoid process</u> and the superior scapular border

* The superior transverse ligament converts the notch into the suprascapular foramen, through which the <u>suprascapular nerve</u> passes.

* Glenoid fossa

* A shallow, <u>concave</u>, anterolaterally directed oval fossa located on the superolateral border of the <u>scapula</u>

* Articulates with the <u>head of the humerus</u> to form the <u>glenohumeral joint</u>

* The supraglenoid tubercle, where the <u>glenohumeral ligament</u> attaches, is located just above the <u>glenoid fossa</u>.





![Scapula (anatomical)](media/ry183hnxc08deuye3ymozqw4.jpg)

Scapula (anatomical)

## Joints of the shoulder girdle

### Sternoclavicular joint  [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




* Definition

* A <u>saddle joint</u> between the <u>medial</u> end of the <u>clavicle</u> and the <u>manubrium</u> <u>sternum</u>

* The only anatomical (true) <u>joint</u> connecting the <u>shoulder girdle</u> to the <u>axial skeleton</u>

* <u>Ligaments</u>

* Anterior sternoclavicular ligament and posterior sternoclavicular ligament

* Between the <u>manubrium</u> and the sternal end of the <u>clavicle</u>

* Strengthens the <u>joint capsule</u> anteriorly and posteriorly and prevents displacement of the <u>clavicle</u>

* Interclavicular ligament

* Unites the sternal ends of both clavicles

* Strengthens the <u>joint capsule</u> superiorly

* Costoclavicular ligament

* Unites the first <u>rib</u> to the sternal end of the <u>clavicle</u>

* Limits elevation of the <u>shoulder girdle</u>

* Movements

* Elevation and <u>depression</u>

* <u>Protraction</u> and <u>retraction</u>

* <u>Circumduction</u>





![Bones and ligaments of the sternoclavicular and sternocostal joints](media/awqu5xonj4dv7a8uhu2z4dq4.jpg)

Bones and ligaments of the sternoclavicular and sternocostal joints




### Acromioclavicular joint (<u>AC joint</u>)  [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




* Definition: : a synovial <u>plane joint</u> between the <u>lateral</u> end of the <u>clavicle</u> and the <u>acromion</u> of the <u>scapula</u>

* <u>Ligaments</u>

* Acromioclavicular ligament

* Extends between the <u>acromion</u> and the <u>clavicle</u>

* Strengthens the superior aspect of the <u>joint capsule</u>

* Resists anteroposterior <u>AC joint displacement</u>

* Coracoclavicular ligament

* Extends between the <u>coracoid process</u> of the <u>scapula</u> and the <u>lateral</u> end of the <u>clavicle</u>

* Divided into the conoid ligament (<u>medial</u>) and trapezoid ligament (<u>lateral</u>)

* Resists rotational and vertical <u>AC joint displacement</u>

* Movements

* No muscles act specifically at the <u>AC joint</u>.

* Anteroposterior and rotational movement is possible with movement of the <u>scapulothoracic joint</u>.





![Anatomy of the capsuloligamentous complex](media/svg34ne2n1ca3lg5wj3y561l.jpg)

Anatomy of the capsuloligamentous complex




### Scapulothoracic joint  [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




* Type of <u>joint</u>

* A physiological rather than an anatomical <u>joint</u>

* The term <u>scapulothoracic joint</u> refers to the movement of the <u>scapula</u> relative to the associated muscles and the thoracic wall.

* Movements of the <u>scapula</u> (<u>scapulothoracic joint</u>)

* Elevation: <u>trapezius</u> (upper part), <u>levator scapulae</u>, and the <u>rhomboid muscles</u>

* <u>Depression</u>: gravity, <u>trapezius</u> (lower fibers), <u>pectoralis minor</u>, and <u>serratus anterior</u>

* <u>Protraction</u> (scapular <u>abduction</u>): <u>serratus anterior</u>, <u>pectoralis major</u>, and <u>pectoralis minor</u>

* <u>Retraction</u> (scapular <u>adduction</u>): <u>trapezius</u> (middle part), <u>latissimus dorsi</u>, and the <u>rhomboid muscles</u>

* <u>Lateral</u> (upward) rotation: <u>serratus anterior</u>, <u>trapezius</u> (upper and lower part)

* <u>Medial</u> (downward) rotation: <u>latissimus dorsi</u>, <u>levator scapulae</u>, <u>pectoralis minor</u>, and <u>rhomboid muscles</u>





![Joints of the shoulder girdle](media/ctm6fk9xz4ddb17n69eitkk7.jpg)

Joints of the shoulder girdle




### <u>Shoulder joint</u> (glenohumeral joint) [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




* Type of <u>joint</u>: <u>ball-and-socket joint</u> between the <u>head of the humerus</u> and the <u>glenoid cavity</u> of the <u>scapula</u>

* Structures  

* Glenoid labrum: a <u>fibrocartilaginous</u> rim surrounding the <u>glenoid fossa</u>

* <u>Joint capsule</u>

* <u>Fibrous layer</u>

* Envelops the entire <u>joint</u>

* <u>Medial</u> attachment: margin of <u>glenoid fossa</u>

* <u>Lateral</u> attachment: <u>anatomical neck of the humerus</u>

* Reinforced superiorly by the <u>rotator cuff</u> muscles and the <u>long head of the biceps</u> brachii

* Weakest inferiorly

* Inner layer: <u>synovial membrane</u>

* Coracoacromial arch

* Forms a protective arch over the <u>glenohumeral joint</u>

* Composed of the following structures:

* <u>Acromion</u>

* <u>Coracoid process</u>

* <u>Coracoacromial ligament</u>

* <u>Ligaments</u>  

* Coracoacromial ligament

* Extends from the <u>coracoid process</u> to the <u>acromion</u>

* Together with the <u>coracoid process</u> and the <u>acromion</u>, it forms the <u>coracoacromial arch</u>, which prevents superior displacement of the <u>humeral head</u> from the <u>glenoid fossa</u>.

* Coracohumeral ligament

* Extends from the <u>coracoid process</u> to the <u>greater tubercle of the humerus</u>

* Strengthens the <u>anterior</u> part of the <u>joint capsule</u>

* Glenohumeral ligament

* Extends from the <u>glenoid labrum</u> at the <u>supraglenoid tubercle</u> of the <u>scapula</u> to the <u>anatomical neck of the humerus</u>

* Strengthens the <u>anterior</u> part of the <u>joint capsule</u>

* Transverse humeral ligament

* Extends from the <u>greater tubercle of the humerus</u> to the <u>lesser tubercle of the humerus</u>

* Bridges the <u>bicipital groove</u> and holds the <u>biceps</u> <u>tendon</u> in place

* <u>Bursae</u>

* Subacromial bursa 

* Synovial fluid-filled sac

* Lies between the <u>acromion</u>, <u>coracoacromial ligament</u>, and <u>deltoid muscle</u> superiorly, and between the <u>shoulder joint</u> capsule and <u>supraspinatus</u> <u>tendon</u> inferiorly

* Does not communicate with the <u>shoulder joint</u> cavity

* Facilitates smooth gliding movement of the <u>supraspinatus</u> <u>tendon</u> and <u>deltoid muscle</u>

* Other <u>bursae</u> are the subscapular, subcoracoid, subscapular recess, coracoclavicular and supraacromial <u>bursae</u>.

* Movements of the <u>shoulder joint</u>  

* <u>Flexion</u> and extension

* <u>Medial</u> and <u>lateral</u> rotation

* <u>Abduction</u> and <u>adduction</u>

* For further details, see “<u>Orthopedic shoulder examination</u>.”





> [!NOTE]
> The <u>head of the humerus</u> is approximately four times larger than the <u>glenoid fossa</u>. The relative size of the <u>humerus</u> allows for a greater <u>range of motion</u> but also increases <u>joint</u> instability.

## Muscles of the shoulder girdle

### Overview [[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




The muscles of the <u>proximal</u> upper limb can be distinguished according to their attachments:




* Scapulohumeral muscles

* Axioappendicular muscles

* <u>Anterior</u> axioappendicular muscles

* <u>Posterior</u> axioappendicular muscles





The movements of the <u>scapula</u> and <u>glenohumeral joint</u> are also supported by the muscles of the arm, such as the <u>triceps</u> and <u>biceps brachii muscles</u> (see “<u>Upper arm and elbow</u>”).




![Shoulder movement](media/hy86riiyuyuexvrsk1awke5f.jpg)

Shoulder movement




### Scapulohumeral (intrinsic shoulder) muscles [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)



* Six muscles originate from the <u>scapula</u> and insert into the <u>humerus</u>:

* <u>Rotator cuff</u> muscles  

* The <u>rotator cuff</u> muscles are responsible for providing the <u>glenohumeral joint</u> with stability and mobility.

* The <u>tendons</u> of the <u>rotator cuff</u> muscles surround the <u>head of the humerus</u> from all sides and hold the <u>humeral head</u> to the articular surface of the <u>scapula</u>.

* The <u>deltoid muscle</u> rests on the <u>rotator cuff</u>.

* The contour of the shoulder is formed mainly by the <u>deltoid muscle</u>.

* See “<u>Examination of the rotator cuff</u>.”

* <u>Teres major muscle</u>: forms the inferior border of the <u>quadrangular space</u>




| Scapulohumeral muscles |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Muscle |  | <br>Origin <br> | <br>Insertion <br> | Innervation | <br>Function <br> |
| Rotator cuff | Supraspinatus muscle | <br>* <u>Supraspinous fossa</u> of the <u>scapula</u><br><br> | <br>* <u>Greater tubercle of the humerus</u><br><br> | <br>* <u>Suprascapular nerve</u><br><br> | <br><br>* Initiation of arm <u>abduction</u> (from 0°–15°)<br><br>* <u>Physical examination</u> via <u>Jobe test</u><br><br><br> |
| Infraspinatus muscle | <br>* <u>Infraspinous fossa</u> of the <u>scapula</u><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>External rotation</u><br><br>* <u>Physical examination</u> via <u>infraspinatus test</u><br><br><br> |  |  |  |
| Teres minor muscle | <br>* Axillary (<u>lateral</u>) border of the <u>scapula</u><br><br> | <br>* <u>Axillary nerve</u><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Adduction</u><br><br>* <u>External rotation</u><br><br><br> |  |  |
| Subscapularis muscle | <br>* <u>Subscapular fossa</u><br><br> | <br>* <u>Lesser tubercle of the humerus</u><br><br> | <br>* Upper and <u>lower subscapular nerves</u><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Adduction</u><br><br>* <u>Internal rotation</u><br><br>* <u>Physical examination</u> via <u>lift-off test</u> or <u>belly-press test</u><br><br><br> |  |

> [!NOTE]
> “roTISSerie:” Teres minor, Infraspinatus, Supraspinatus, and Subscapularis are the muscles of the rotator cuff.

### <u>Anterior</u> axioappendicular muscles [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




* <u>Subclavius muscle</u>: depresses the shoulder and <u>lateral</u> end of the <u>clavicle</u>

* <u>Pectoralis major muscle</u>  

* Shoulder <u>adduction</u>, <u>internal rotation</u>, and <u>anteversion</u>

* Draws <u>scapula</u> anteriorly and inferiorly

* <u>Accessory muscle of respiration</u>

* <u>Pectoralis minor muscle</u> 

* Stabilizes <u>scapula</u> (draws it anteriorly and inferiorly against the thoracic wall)

* <u>Accessory muscle of respiration</u>

* <u>Serratus anterior muscle</u> 

* <u>Scapula</u>: <u>protraction</u>

* Inferior angle of the <u>scapula</u>: upward rotation

* Maintains position of the inferomedial <u>scapula</u> against the thoracic wall

* <u>Abduction</u> of the arm (> 100°)

* <u>Accessory muscle of respiration</u>

* See “<u>Upper arm and elbow</u>.”





> [!NOTE]
> SALT: The Serratus Anterior muscle is innervated by the Long Thoracic nerve.

### <u>Posterior</u> axioappendicular (extrinsic shoulder) muscles [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




* <u>Superficial</u> extrinsic shoulder muscles

* <u>Trapezius muscle</u> 

* Descending part

* <u>Scapula</u> elevation and upward rotation

* <u>Overhead</u> <u>abduction</u> of the arm (> 90°)

* Transverse part: <u>scapula</u> <u>adduction</u> (i.e., pulls the <u>scapula</u> medially)

* Ascending part: <u>scapula</u> <u>depression</u>

* <u>Latissimus dorsi muscle</u> 

* <u>Adducts</u>, extends, and <u>internally rotates</u> the arm

* <u>Accessory muscle of respiration</u>

* Deep extrinsic shoulder muscles

* Levator scapulae muscle 

* <u>Scapula</u> elevation (shrugging)

* In conjunction with the <u>rhomboid muscles</u>: returns the elevated arm to its neutral position

* <u>Rhomboid major muscle</u> and <u>rhomboid minor muscle</u> 

* <u>Scapula</u> elevation and <u>retraction</u>

* <u>Lateral</u> angle of the <u>scapula</u>: <u>caudal</u> rotation





See “<u>Superficial back muscles</u>.”

## The axilla

### Overview   [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




* Definition

* A three-dimensional, pyramid-shaped area at the junction of the arm and thorax

* Inferior to the <u>shoulder joint</u>, through which important vessels and nerves pass from the trunk to the arm

* Boundaries

* Apex

* Also called the cervicoaxillary canal or axillary inlet

* Bounded by the <u>lateral</u> border of the 1<sup>st</sup><u>rib</u>, the superior border of the <u>scapula</u>, and the <u>clavicle</u>

* Vessels and <u>lymphatics</u> pass through this opening to and from the arm.

* <u>Anterior</u> wall: <u>pectoralis major</u> and <u>pectoralis minor</u> muscles

* <u>Posterior</u> wall: <u>latissimus dorsi</u>, <u>teres major</u>, and <u>subscapularis</u> muscles, and the <u>scapula</u>

* <u>Lateral</u> wall: <u>coracobrachialis muscle</u> and the <u>humerus</u>

* <u>Medial</u> wall: <u>serratus anterior</u>, the 1<sup>st</sup>–4<sup>th</sup><u>ribs</u>, and the <u>intercostal muscles</u>

* Base

* Formed by <u>skin</u>, <u>subcutaneous tissue</u>, and axillary <u>fascia</u>

* Also known as the axillary fossa or armpit

* Bounded externally by the <u>anterior</u> and <u>posterior</u> axillary folds

* Contents 

* <u>Axillary artery</u> and its branches

* <u>Axillary vein</u> and its tributaries

* <u>Axillary lymph node groups</u> and lymphatic vessels

* <u>Brachial plexus</u>

* Axillary fat and <u>connective tissue</u>





> [!NOTE]
> The <u>anterior</u> axillary fold is formed from the <u>pectoralis major muscle</u>. The <u>posterior</u> axillary fold is formed from the <u>latissimus dorsi</u> and <u>teres major</u> muscles.




![Axillary fossa](media/ge2ggm5q36tx5vj437qh3jxa.jpg)

Axillary fossa




### Axillary spaces  [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)



* Definition: anatomical spaces (2 triangular, 1 quadrangular) bound by the <u>teres minor muscle</u> (cranially) and the <u>teres major muscle</u> (<u>caudally</u>), through which structures leave the <u>axilla</u>




![The three axillary spaces (dorsal view)](media/heuniqz8v398i3v28hcjs52h.jpg)

The three axillary spaces (dorsal view)




#### Medial triangular space (<u>upper triangular space</u>)




* Shape: a <u>triangular space</u> with a <u>cranial</u>, <u>caudal</u>, and <u>lateral</u> border and apex inferomedially (i.e., no <u>medial</u> border)

* Borders 

* <u>Cranial</u>: <u>teres minor muscle</u>

* <u>Caudal</u>: <u>teres major muscle</u>

* <u>Lateral</u>: <u>triceps brachii muscle</u> (long head)

* Structures within: <u>circumflex scapular artery</u> and <u>vein</u>





#### Triangular interval (<u>lower triangular space</u>)




* Shape: a <u>triangular space</u> with a <u>cranial</u>, <u>lateral</u>, and <u>medial</u> border and apex inferiorly (i.e., no <u>caudal</u> border)

* Borders

* <u>Cranial</u>: <u>teres major muscle</u>

* <u>Lateral</u>: <u>humerus</u>

* <u>Medial</u>: <u>triceps brachii muscle</u> (long head)

* Structures within

* <u>Deep brachial artery</u>

* <u>Radial nerve</u>





#### Quadrangular space




* Shape: a <u>quadrangular space</u> that allows access to the <u>posterior</u> arm and shoulder area

* Borders

* <u>Cranial</u>: <u>teres minor muscle</u>

* <u>Caudal</u>: <u>teres major muscle</u>

* <u>Medial</u>: <u>triceps brachii</u> (long head)

* <u>Lateral</u>: <u>humerus</u>

* Structures within

* <u>Posterior humeral circumflex artery</u> and <u>vein</u>

* <u>Axillary nerve</u>





> [!NOTE]
> A simple trick for remembering the structures at the borders of the <u>axillary spaces</u> is to simulate them with the middle and index fingers of both hands. Form a peace sign with both hands and superimpose them at ∼ 90°. Three spaces are created. These represent the <u>axillary spaces</u>.




![Visual mnemonic: Axillary spaces and their borders](media/xose06bfciel2cl7g5068n3i.jpg)

Visual mnemonic: Axillary spaces and their borders

## Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage

### Arterial supply   [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




#### Axillary artery [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




* Origin: continuation of the <u>subclavian artery</u> at the outer border of the 1<sup>st</sup><u>rib</u>

* Course

* In the <u>axilla</u>, it lies <u>lateral</u> to the <u>axillary vein</u>.

* Continues as the <u>brachial artery</u> at the outer border of the <u>teres major</u>

* Divided into 3 parts by the overlying <u>pectoralis minor muscle</u>

* 1<sup>st</sup> part: <u>proximal</u> to the <u>pectoralis minor</u>

* 2<sup>nd</sup> part: inferior to the <u>pectoralis minor</u>

* 3<sup>rd</sup> part: <u>distal</u> to the <u>pectoralis minor</u>





| Branches of the <u>axillary artery</u> |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | Origin | Course | Supplies |
| Superior thoracic artery | <br>* 1<sup>st</sup> part<br><br> | <br><br>* Runs anteromedially along the superior border of the <u>pectoralis minor</u> before passing between it and the <u>pectoralis major</u> to reach the thoracic wall<br><br>* Forms <u>anastomoses</u> with the <u>intercostal arteries</u> and the <u>internal thoracic artery</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* 1<sup>st</sup> and 2<sup>nd</sup> <u>intercostal muscles</u><br><br>* Superior part of the <u>serratus anterior muscle</u><br><br>* Pectoral muscles<br><br>* <u>Subclavius muscle</u><br><br>* <u>Skin</u> of the thoracic wall<br><br><br> |
| <br>Thoracoacromial artery (<u>thoracoacromial trunk</u>) | <br>* 2<sup>nd</sup> part (first branch)<br><br> | <br><br>* Runs <u>posterior</u> to the <u>pectoralis minor muscle</u> before piercing the clavipectoral fascia<br><br>* Divides into four branches:<br><br>* Pectoral branch<br><br>* Deltoid branch<br><br>* Acromial branch<br><br>* Clavicular branch<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Pectoral muscles<br><br>* <u>Deltoid muscle</u><br><br>* <u>Skin</u> overlying the <u>clavipectoral fascia</u><br><br><br> |
| <br>Lateral thoracic artery<br> | <br>* 2<sup>nd</sup> part (second branch)<br><br> | <br>* Descends along the axillary border of the <u>pectoralis minor</u><br><br> | <br>* <u>Lateral</u> structures of the thorax and the <u>breast</u><br><br> |
| Anterior humeral circumflex artery | <br>* 3<sup>rd</sup> part<br><br> | <br><br>* Passes laterally deep to the <u>coracobrachialis</u> and <u>biceps brachii muscles</u><br><br>* Gives off an ascending branch, which runs inside the <u>intertubercular sulcus</u><br><br>* Forms <u>anastomoses</u> with the <u>posterior humeral circumflex artery</u> <u>lateral</u> to the <u>humerus</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Glenohumeral joint</u><br><br>* <u>Teres major</u>, <u>teres minor</u>, and <u>deltoid muscles</u><br><br><br> |
| Posterior humeral circumflex artery | <br><br>* Passes through the <u>quadrangular space</u> together with the <u>axillary nerve</u><br><br>* Gives off a descending branch<br><br>* Forms <u>anastomoses</u> with the <u>anterior humeral circumflex artery</u> <u>lateral</u> to the <u>humerus</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Glenohumeral joint</u><br><br>* <u>Teres major</u>, <u>teres minor</u>, <u>triceps</u>, and <u>deltoid muscles</u><br><br><br> |  |
| Subscapular artery | <br><br>* Descends along the <u>lateral</u> border of the <u>subscapularis</u> on the <u>posterior</u> axillary wall<br><br>* Divides into the thoracodorsal <u>artery</u> and the <u>circumflex scapular artery</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* 3 Rotator cuff muscles<br><br>* <u>Subscapularis</u><br><br>* <u>Infraspinatus</u><br><br>* <u>Supraspinatus</u><br><br>* <u>Deltoid muscle</u><br><br>* <u>Latissimus dorsi muscle</u><br><br>* Long head of <u>triceps brachii muscle</u><br><br>* <u>Serratus anterior muscle</u><br><br>* Adjacent <u>skin</u><br><br><br> |  |





![Arteries of the upper extremity](media/pczabpv1mfqwjuigejhxhtfp.jpg)

Arteries of the upper extremity




#### Scapular anastomosis [[2]](/library/XNY9-6)



* Definition: an <u>anastomosis</u> between the branches of the first part of the <u>subclavian artery</u> and the third part of the <u>axillary artery</u> that provides collateral circulation to the arm in case of occlusion or injury to the axillary or <u>subclavian arteries</u>




| Overview of scapular <u>arteries</u> |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <u>Artery</u> | Origin | Location |
| Dorsal scapular artery | <br>* <u>Thyrocervical trunk</u> or a direct branch of the <u>subclavian artery</u><br><br> | <br>* <u>Medial</u> border of the <u>scapula</u><br><br> |
| Suprascapular artery | <br>* <u>Supraspinous fossa</u> of the <u>scapula</u><br><br> |  |
| Circumflex scapular artery | <br>* <u>Subscapular artery</u><br><br> | <br>* <u>Infraspinous fossa</u> of the <u>scapula</u><br><br> |
| <u>Subscapular artery</u> | <br>* 3<sup>rd</sup> part of the <u>axillary artery</u><br><br> | <br>* <u>Lateral</u> border of the <u>scapula</u><br><br> |
| <u>Intercostal arteries</u> | <br>* <u>Subclavian artery</u> or the descending <u>thoracic aorta</u><br><br> | <br>* Multiple <u>anastomoses</u> with the <u>dorsal scapular artery</u> at the <u>medial</u> border of the <u>scapula</u><br><br> |





![image](media/mgyelhn2d756b6aoepc37tj4.jpg)




### Venous drainage   [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)




#### Axillary vein




* Origin: formed at the outer border of the <u>teres major muscle</u> by the union of the <u>basilic vein</u> and the accompanying <u>veins</u> of the <u>brachial artery</u>

* Course

* Runs with the <u>axillary artery</u>

* Divided into 3 sections that correspond to the parts of the <u>axillary artery</u> (the <u>distal</u> end is the first part)

* Continues as the <u>subclavian vein</u> at the <u>lateral</u> border of the 1<sup>st</sup><u>rib</u>

* Tributaries

* Generally correspond to <u>axillary artery</u> tributaries

* Exceptions

* There is no common tributary for the <u>veins</u> that correspond to the branches of the <u>thoracoacromial trunk</u>.

* Directly or indirectly receives the <u>thoracoepigastric veins</u>

* Drains: upper limb, <u>axilla</u>, <u>lateral</u> <u>chest wall</u>





![Veins of the upper extremity](media/bl2j6lljsiu87rm2l3rbn7wd.jpg)

Veins of the upper extremity




### <u>Lymphatic drainage</u> [[1]](/library/ES08Yf)[[2]](/library/XNY9-6)



* Tributaries:

* <u>Lymphatics</u> from the upper limb and upper torso drain into the five <u>axillary lymph node groups</u>.

* Efferent vessels from the apical <u>lymph node group</u> exit via the apex of the <u>axilla</u> and unite to form the subclavian lymphatic trunk, and some vessels also drain into the clavicular nodes.

* See “<u>Axillary lymph nodes</u>.”




![Palpable lymph nodes of the axillary region](media/g0g0kwcszqvotw9znespg3a7.jpg)

Palpable lymph nodes of the axillary region

## Brachial plexus

* Description: a network of nerves derived from the C5–T1 <u>spinal nerves</u> that give rise to the <u>peripheral nerves</u> of the upper limb and shoulder

* Roots  
* <u>Anterior rami</u> of C5–T1 <u>spinal nerves</u> (i.e., five roots)

* Dorsal scapular nerve: arises directly from C5 and innervates the <u>rhomboid major</u>, <u>rhomboid minor</u>, and <u>levator scapulae muscles</u>

* Long thoracic nerve: arises from roots C5, C6, and C7 and innervates the <u>serratus anterior muscle</u>

* The first <u>intercostal nerve</u> arises from T1.

* Trunks
* The roots form three trunks that are located in the neck.

* C5 and C6 form the upper trunk of the brachial plexus: The suprascapular nerve (innervates the <u>infraspinatus</u> and <u>supraspinatus</u> muscles) and nerve to subclavius (innervates the <u>subclavius muscle</u>) originate here.

* C7 forms the middle trunk of the brachial plexus.

* C8 and T1 form the lower trunk of the brachial plexus.

* Divisions: All three trunks separate into an <u>anterior</u> and <u>posterior</u> division that enters into the <u>axillary fossa</u>.

* All three <u>posterior</u> divisions innervate the extensor compartment of the arm and forearm (i.e., the <u>posterior</u> compartment).

* All three <u>anterior</u> divisions innervate the flexor compartment of the arm and forearm (i.e., the <u>anterior</u> compartment).

* Cords

* Only the cords and <u>proximal</u> portions of their branches lie in the <u>axilla</u>.

* There are three cords, which are named according to their position in relation to the <u>axillary artery</u>.

* The <u>anterior</u> divisions of upper and middle trunks form the lateral cord of the brachial plexus.

* The <u>anterior</u> division of the lower trunks forms the medial cord of the brachial plexus.

* The <u>posterior</u> divisions of all the trunks form the posterior cord of the brachial plexus.

* Functional significance

* Motor innervation: all upper limb and shoulder muscles (except for the <u>trapezius</u>, which is supplied by the <u>spinal accessory nerve</u>)

* Sensory innervation: the <u>axilla</u> and upper limb (except for the <u>medial</u> portion of the arm, which is supplied by the <u>intercostobrachial nerve</u>)





| The <u>brachial plexus</u> |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | Branches of the <u>brachial plexus</u> | Spinal roots | Motor innervation | <br>Sensory innervation<br> |
| <u>Lateral cord</u> | <br>Musculocutaneous nerve<br> | <br>* C5–C7<br><br> | <br>* <u>Anterior compartment of the arm</u><br><br>* <u>Biceps</u><br><br>* <u>Brachialis</u><br><br>* <u>Coracobrachialis</u><br><br> | <br>* <u>Lateral</u> aspect of the forearm<br><br> |
| Lateral pectoral nerve | <br>* C5–C7<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Pectoralis major</u><br><br>* Sometimes the <u>pectoralis minor</u><br><br><br> | <br>* None<br><br> |  |
| <u>Lateral root of median nerve</u> | <br>* C5–C7<br><br> | <br><br>* Forearm: all flexors (<u>anterior</u> compartment) except for those supplied by the <u>ulnar nerve</u><br><br>* Hand: <u>thenar muscles</u> and <u>lateral</u> two <u>lumbricals</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Radial ⅔ of the palm<br><br>* <u>Palmar</u> aspect of the radial 3 ½ fingers (i.e., the thumb, index finger, middle finger, and radial side of the ring finger)<br><br>* <u>Dorsal</u> aspect of the <u>distal</u> <u>phalanges</u> of the radial 3 ½ fingers<br><br>* <u>Autonomous sensory zone</u>: tip of the index finger<br><br><br> |  |
| <u>Medial</u> cord | <u>Medial root of median nerve</u> | <br>* C8–T1<br><br> |  |  |
| Medial pectoral nerve | <br><br>* <u>Pectoralis major</u><br><br>* <u>Pectoralis minor</u><br><br><br> | <br>* None<br><br> |  |  |
| <u>Medial cutaneous nerve of arm</u> | <br>* None<br><br> | <br>* Inferomedial aspect of the arm<br><br> |  |  |
| <u>Medial cutaneous nerve of forearm</u> | <br>* None<br><br> | <br>* <u>Skin</u> over the <u>medial</u> forearm<br><br> |  |  |
| <u>Ulnar nerve</u> | <br><br>* Forearm: <u>flexor carpi ulnaris</u> and the <u>medial</u> half of the <u>flexor digitorum profundus</u><br><br>* Hand: all muscles except those supplied by the <u>median nerve</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Ulnar ⅓ of the palm<br><br>* <u>Palmar</u> and <u>dorsal</u> aspects of the ulnar 1 ½ fingers (i.e., the little finger and the ulnar side of the ring finger)<br><br>* <u>Autonomous sensory zone</u>: tip of the little finger<br><br><br> |  |  |
| <u>Posterior cord</u> | Upper subscapular nerve | <br>* C5<br><br> | <br>* <u>Subscapularis</u><br><br> | <br>* None<br><br> |
| Lower subscapular nerve | <br>* C6–C8<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Subscapularis</u><br><br>* <u>Teres major</u><br><br><br> | <br>* None<br><br> |  |
| Thoracodorsal nerve | <br>* C6<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Latissimus dorsi</u><br><br>* Sometimes the <u>teres major</u><br><br><br> | <br>* None<br><br> |  |
| <u>Radial nerve</u> | <br>* C5–T1<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Muscles of the posterior compartment of the arm</u>: <u>triceps brachii</u>, <u>anconeus</u><br><br>* <u>Lateral</u> part of the <u>brachialis</u><br><br>* <u>Posterior compartment of the forearm</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Radial ⅔ of the <u>dorsal</u> aspect of the hand<br><br>* <u>Dorsal</u> aspect of the radial 3 ½ fingers (except the area supplied by the <u>median nerve</u>)<br><br>* <u>Autonomous sensory zone</u>: 1<sup>st</sup> web space (between the thumb and index finger)<br><br><br> |  |
| Axillary nerve | <br>* C5-6<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Shoulder joint</u><br><br>* <u>Teres minor</u><br><br>* <u>Deltoid muscle</u><br><br><br> | <br>* <u>Skin</u> of the superolateral arm (over the inferior part of the <u>deltoid muscle</u>)<br><br> |  |





> [!NOTE]
> Branches from the <u>medial</u> and <u>lateral</u> cords form the <u>median nerve</u>.




> [!NOTE]
> “Rugby Teams Drink Cool Beer!” (Roots, Trunks, Divisions, Cords, Branches is the order of the <u>brachial plexus</u> divisions)

* <u>Thoracic outlet syndrome</u>

* Bones and <u>joints</u>

* <u>Clavicle fracture</u>

* <u>Shoulder dislocation</u>

* <u>Acromioclavicular joint injury</u>

* <u>Soft tissue lesions of the shoulder</u>

* <u>Subacromial impingement syndrome</u>

* <u>Rotator cuff tendinitis</u>

* <u>Rotator cuff tear</u>

* <u>Subacromial bursitis</u>

* <u>Subclavian steal syndrome</u>

* <u>Frozen shoulder</u> (<u>adhesive capsulitis</u>)

* <u>Biceps tendinopathy</u>

* <u>Nerve injuries in the upper body</u>

* <u>Suprascapular nerve injury</u>

* <u>Erb palsy</u>

* <u>Klumpke palsy</u>

* <u>Axillary nerve injury</u>

* <u>Long thoracic nerve injury</u> (<u>Winged scapula</u>)

* <u>Pancoast tumor</u>
